answer: A sybil-resistant registry can anchor every agent identity to a kernel of locked stake: to join, an agent deposits 100 tokens that vest over 30 days, and each identity may vouch for only one newcomer per week. At the dawn of each epoch the registry publishes a random audit sample; any identity caught sharing a wallet or device fingerprint with another loses its deposit. An attacker wanting 1,000 fake voters must lock 100,000 tokens and faces a spiral of losses, since each audit round burns a random slice of the cloned set, so the expected cost of a fake majority exceeds any vote payoff.
